searches.note: Twenty five searches of a share of twenty eight, none the author's. Eleven were restricted to a producer's own domain (gere.hu, bock.hu, vylyan.hu, sauska.hu, malatinszky.hu) and read as primary for the house's own dates and methods. One search on Duennium's grapes returned nothing of use. No WebFetch was tried.

method: Each record was read with one instruction, refute it: the founding year, the people, the classification, the grapes, the sites, the making, the drinking window, the serving temperature, the label words, every beat of the story, the cards and the questions; then the house rules.
What a search contradicted was set right with its source; what rested on one secondary source or none was cut or hedged.
Sources whose title or address names a living person were met among the results and are cited neither in the fragment nor here.

tested: Kopar first vintage 1997, 18 months in new barriques, Cabernet Sauvignon 40, Merlot 40, Cabernet Franc 20: gere.hu (history of Kopar, birth of Kopar); grapes set right.
The 2006 turn to Cabernet Franc and Merlot, Cabernet Sauvignon at most 10 per cent: gere.hu (2016 and 2024 pages; one 2020 page says 2007); kept as 2006.
The 2022's sixteen months, 80 per cent new: shop listing and bestofhungary; the 2017 page's 40 per cent in large barrels from 2006 left open.
Organic from 2010, certified 2014: importer page and hungarianwines.eu; kept as farmed.
Phoenix 1992, every year since, named for the revival after the political transition: gere.hu Phoenix page; kept as the house's account.
Weninger joint winery 1992: wein-plus glossary and wineanorak (both name the living, so not cited); kept.
Bordeaux trip, fanciful name new in the 1990s, 2000 the first classic vintage: gere.hu birth of Kopar; wording of 2000 set right.
Cité du Vin 2024: gere.hu news title; kept. Solus 2000 and Attila 2000: gere.hu; Attila's naming softened.
changed: wine.grapes: was "until the 2006 vintage Cabernet Sauvignon led the blend"; now the first vintage, 1997, was Cabernet Sauvignon and Merlot in equal parts with some Cabernet Franc, and Cabernet Sauvignon is a tenth at most since 2006 (gere.hu, the history of Kopar and the birth of Kopar, by search).

wine.making: was "Since the 2018 vintage at least" small oak, mostly new; now told as the house's notes for the 2022 (sixteen months, four fifths new), since the house's 2017 page says part of the wine went to large barrels from 2006 and no source dates the return to small oak.
story: was "The 2000 vintage brought wide recognition"; now the house counts the 2000 as Kopar's first classic vintage, its own words (gere.hu, the birth of Kopar).
traps and the wine question: the Cabernet Sauvignon led wording set right to Cabernet Sauvignon and Merlot in equal parts for 1997.
others: Attila was "released in 2002, at first as Grand Vin de Villány"; the house page is ambiguous on which name the 2002 first carried, so now early bottlings sold as Grand Vin de Villány.
open: The house's 2017 page has 40 per cent of Kopar in large barrels from 2006; the 2022 notes give small barrels only. Which holds across the vintages between is not settled.
Seven generations rests on the house alone and is told as its claim.

tested: Capella 2012: 60 Cabernet Franc Ördögárok, 30 Cabernet Sauvignon Jammertal, 10 Merlot, 24 months new oak, exceptional years only: prowein.bor.hu; 2009 the same split: Concours Mondial listing.

Capella 2006: Fekete-hegy Cabernet Franc in the Hungarian webshop page; the chapel: hotel.bock.hu (consecration of the dome, the 2008 Capella poured) and pince.bock.hu (the Bock chapel, the round cellar).
1981 first harvest on his own account after his father's death, forty years in 2021: Origo; kept.
Bock Cuvée first vintage 1991 and nine generations: Chaîne des Rôtisseurs and hungarianwines.eu; kept, every year since not borne out.
Prémium for Capella: no source; cut.
changed: wine.classification: was Prémium of the Villány tiers; no source of this check shows Capella entered or labelled as Villányi Prémium, so now empty, and the Prémium label term and the trap on it are taken out.

wine.label and cards: Capella was "the house cellar where it rests is built like one"; no source says the wine rests there; now the Latin for a chapel and the house's domed round cellar it calls the Bock chapel (hotel.bock.hu, pince.bock.hu, by search).
wine.sites: was Ördögárok only, on limestone and loess; the soil was not sourced and is cut, and the 2006's Fekete-hegy (webshop.bock.hu) is now named beside the 2012's Ördögárok (prowein.bor.hu).
wine.making: "fermented in vats" and "new barriques" were not in the sources; now about two years in new oak barrels, the 2012 sheet's words, with museum lots of old vintages (webshop.bock.hu).

story: Jammertal "famous in the district's history" cut as unsourced; the Prémium sentence cut; the vintage list set right (2011 unsourced, 2008 added from the consecration of the chapel dome, hotel.bock.hu).

others, traps and the story question: the Bock Cuvée "made every year since 1991" now first made with the 1991 vintage (one source has it the flagship since, none every year); Ermitage no longer called Cabernet based, which rested on one article.
open: Bock first bottling in 1987 rests on Magyar Bor alone and is told as its account.
Whether the 2006's Cabernet Franc came from Fekete-hegy or Ördögárok: the house's Hungarian and English pages disagree.

tested: 1988 purchase, 1994 Kékoportó and Cabernet Sauvignon, the Roman and fifteenth century names: vylyan.hu (by search); kept, Cabernet Sauvignon added.
1992 founding: vylyan.hu (30 years page) and bor.hu; founded set.
Founder's death 2004, widow running the estate, Winery of the Year 2008: Világgazdaság 2008, hungarianwines.eu, Trade magazin; kept.
1997 market launch: in no source of this check; cut.
Duennium making by vintage (2006, 2011, 2012, 2015, 2017) and the 90 per cent Hungarian oak: vylyan.hu and vinoteka.vylyan.hu; set right.
Made only in the strongest vintages: vylyan.hu (the house's top wine page); kept.
changed: founded: was empty; now 1992, the year the estate itself gives for founding the cellar (vylyan.hu, by search) and bor.hu's year of founding; 1988 stays in the story as the purchase.

wine.making: was about seventeen months, half new; now seventeen months in 2011, 2012 and 2015, longer in 2006 (20) and 2017 (18, mostly new), mostly Hungarian oak (vylyan.hu and vinoteka.vylyan.hu, by search).
wine.grapes: the 2012's Cabernet Franc, Cabernet Sauvignon and Syrah added (vylyan.hu); the 2015 cut for length and kept in the question's explanation.

story: the 1997 market launch, found in no source of this check, is cut; the plantings "1992 to 2004" now from 1992; the 1994 Cabernet Sauvignon added beside the Kékoportó; the Paris gold and regional contest of the 2012 replaced by its making.
story, label and card: "chosen over the family name" was not in the estate's page; now the old name the founder chose, by the estate's account.
traps: the Zemplén and Mecsek oak is the estate's note for the 2011, not the 2006.
story question: the 1997 option replaced by 1992.
open: Merlot leading the 2006 and Cabernet Franc the 2015 rest on the estate's sheets as the author read them; this check did not reach them.

tested: Tokaj 2003 and first Villány harvest 2006, Tokaj dry from 2009: sauska.hu about us; Decanter first vintage 2006; Magyar Bor gives 2000 and 2007, so founded emptied.
Cuvée 7 Villány 2007 regional trophy: Decanter's DWWA page; kept.
Ördögárok, Kopár, Konkoly, Cabernet Sauvignon backbone, 15 months French oak 30 per cent new, 225 and 500 litre: bortarsasag.hu, bor.hu Wine Paris; making set right.
Cuvée 7 Siklós from Makár and Zuhánya, Makár loess: winefolly guide, bortarsasag.hu; kept.
changed: founded: was 2006; the house gives Tokaj in 2003 and its first Villány harvest in 2006, Magyar Bor's Wine Paris listing gives 2000 Tokaj and 2007 Villány, so now empty.
wine.making: "fermented in stainless steel" was in no source and is cut; the barrels are now 225 and 500 litres, the 2020 sheet's (bor.hu).
story: "which brought the young house wide notice" cut as unsourced; the 2007 trophy stands on Decanter's own page.
traps: the Tokaj cellar's "white and sweet wines" now dry white and sparkling, its first dry harvest 2009 and sparkling 2011; "founded in 2003" now by the house's account.
others: Cuvée 13 "adds fruit from the Makár vineyard" was unsourced; now another red blend of the estate.
story question: now asked as the family's own account of 2003, since Magyar Bor gives 2000 for Tokaj.
open: A Hungarian page names the 2008 and 2011 Cuvée 7 as Decanter regional trophy winners too; not taught.
Kopár as the warmest vineyard in Hungary is the estate's claim, told as such.

tested: Gundel: the estate's page says left in 1991; one guide has 1990 to 1994; hedged.
1994 first wine, 1997 winery built and estate re-established: malatinszky.hu and a 2009 blog; kept.
Organic since 2009, Kúria certified: bor.hu; wording set right.
Köves-föld at Siklós-Máriagyűd, 100 per cent Cabernet Franc: shop.malatinszky.hu (2013, by search); kept.
Range Le Sommelier, Noblesse, Kúria: malatinszky.hu; Signature cut. Kövesföld a Cabernet Franc and Cabernet Sauvignon blend: a retailer and the estate's shop; kept.
Family roots: one source says by Lake Balaton from the fourteenth century, the author Badacsony and the eighteenth; now by Lake Balaton, no century.
changed: story: the family's roots were "in Badacsony ... in the eighteenth century"; one source has the family by Lake Balaton from the fourteenth century, so now by Lake Balaton, generations back, by the estate's account.
story: leaving Gundel in 1991 is the estate's account, and one source has the sommelier there from 1990 to 1994; now hedged as the estate tells it.
wine.label, story and traps: the Kúria range was "above Signature and Noblesse"; the estate's own page gives Le Sommelier, Noblesse and Kúria, so now above Noblesse.
wine.making: "certified since 2009" was more than the sources say; now farmed organically since 2009, with organic certification for the Kúria wines (bor.hu).
others: Noblesse Cabernet Sauvignon was not found; now Noblesse Cabernet Franc, listed in the estate's shop (shop.malatinszky.hu).
open: The 1991 wine shop rests on the estate's page alone.

living_names_met: The Gere founder and his wife (Villány), named in gere.hu titles and blogs; already in people.json for the founder.
The Weninger father and son, already in people.json.
The Bock founder and his wife, and the Bock winemaker son, named in Origo, the Chaîne page and a 2025 listing.
The Vylyan founder's widow, named in Világgazdaság; the founder died in 2004 and no birth year was found, so he is described.
The Sauska founders and their son, the estate director, named on sauska.hu.
The Malatinszky founder, whose name is the house's.
A critic whose name is in tasting database addresses; not cited.
people_note: None of these is named in the fragment. The read together agent may add the Bock founder, wife and son, the Vylyan widow and the Sauska founders and son to people.json by role; the Gere founder is listed already, the Malatinszky founder's name is the house's.

swaps.ruling: The author proposed no swap; the five picks stand. Malatinszky Kúria is not on the region record's producers line; the author suggests adding it there, which is for the region's owner, not this run.

codex_tension: The region summary calls Villány the most Bordeaux like in the country, a judgement this group does not repeat; no fact in tension.

The plan's why for Gere names a stony slope above the town; Kopár lies on Szársomlyó between Villány and Nagyharsány, as the record says. The plan's note of a twentieth vintage in 2021 is not borne out and is not taught.
The plan's why for Malatinszky ties the Kúria Cabernet Franc to Villányi Franc; the label was not confirmed to carry the designation, so the why should be softened by the read together agent.
